title: Confidentiality of the recovery and monitoring program record and the director's reports to the licensing board
rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 112, § 65G(a) the record of participation is the materials received and reviewed by the program's director, rehabilitation evaluation committee or a licensing board in connection with a licensed health care professional's application for admission and with a participant's progress and compliance with an individualized rehabilitation plan. Under § 65G(h) the record of participation shall not be a public record and is exempt from disclosure under clause Twenty-sixth of section 7 of chapter 4 and chapter 66. If a licensed health care professional referred to the program by a licensing board fails to complete the application process, a licensing board may use information and documents in the record of participation as evidence in a disciplinary proceeding as necessary to protect public health, safety and welfare; in all other instances the record of participation or application to the program shall be kept confidential and shall not be subject to subpoena or discovery in any civil, criminal, legislative or administrative proceeding without the prior written consent of the participant or applicant. Upon the rehabilitation evaluation committee's determination that a participant has successfully completed the program and that the participant's ability to safely practice is not impaired or affected by mental health or substance use, the department, the program, the committee and the licensing board, if applicable, shall seal all records pertaining to the participant's participation, and the records of participation of participants who successfully complete the program shall be destroyed 3 years following the date of successful completion. Under § 65G(e)(viii), where an applicant or participant is referred to the program by a licensing board, or is the subject of a pending or completed investigation or complaint that arises from or relates to the applicant's or participant's mental health or substance use, the director shall report to the licensing board the name and license number of the applicant or participant in the event of the applicant's failure to complete the admission process, the participant's admission, termination or withdrawal before completion, and the initial restrictions or conditions relating to professional practice in the individualized rehabilitation plan together with any changes to or removal of them and the basis for them.
exam_relevance: Tests what the statute's confidentiality protects and where it stops: evidentiary use after a board-referred applicant fails to complete the application, disclosure with written consent, the director's reports of name and license number, and sealing and destruction after successful completion.

numeric_facts.fact: destruction of the records of participation of a participant who successfully completes the program
numeric_facts.conditions: following the date of successful completion

exceptions: A licensing board may use information and documents in the record of participation as evidence in a disciplinary proceeding, as necessary to protect public health, safety and welfare, where a professional referred by a licensing board fails to complete the application process
The bar on subpoena and discovery yields to the prior written consent of the participant or applicant
common_confusions: Confidentiality of the record does not stop the director reporting a name and license number to the licensing board where the professional was referred by the board or is the subject of a related investigation or complaint.
Sealing follows the rehabilitation evaluation committee's determination of successful completion; destruction follows 3 years after the date of successful completion.
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-16 in the current text of M.G.L. c. 112, § 65G on malegislature.gov.
